title: Warm Capacity Subscriptions — Product Brief & Pricing
author: Aisha Chen
body:
Summary:

This product brief describes Warm Capacity Subscriptions (a.k.a. Warm Pools), a new add-on for Dedicated and Private customers that guarantees a configurable pool of pre-warmed model-serving slots to reduce cold-start latency and provide predictable tail latency for bursty traffic patterns. The doc covers the product rationale, target personas, technical design constraints, pricing model, SLO/SLA impacts, launch plan, and required implementation deliverables.

Problem statement:

Many enterprise customers integrating LLM inference experience high tail latency or transient errors when traffic spikes or when infrequently used model variants are rotated onto GPUs. The existing Dedicated reserved capacity reduces this risk, but small or variable workloads still face cold-starts caused by model loading, compilation, or quantized kernel warm-up. Customers building interactive experiences (chat, code-assist, search) require >95th-percentile latency stability and explicit cost controls for standing warm capacity.

Goals (Success criteria):

- Reduce 95th/99th percentile cold-start latency for targeted routes by at least 60% versus baseline without warm capacity.
- Provide a predictable pricing model customers can purchase monthly/annual for standing warm capacity.
- Integrate with existing Dedicated autoscaling and Private on-prem packaging without requiring service interruption.
- Provide telemetry, usage reporting, and cost attribution per-tenant and per-route.

Target users / buyer personas:

- Platform engineers at SaaS companies deploying interactive LLM features (chat, autocomplete, code gen).
- Enterprise procurement/staff who prefer predictable monthly committed spend for critical latency guarantees.
- Solutions engineers who onboard customers with compliance or audit requirements and must prove latency stability.

Product overview (How it works):

- Warm Pool: a named subscription of N warm slots (N GPUs or vCPU-backed serving slots depending on deployment) that are continuously kept ready for fast assignment. Each slot is associated with a set of allowed model families and sequence-length templates.
- Assignment & Routing: Smart routing reserves a warm slot for a matching route when request rate or a scheduled reservation occurs. If no matching warm slot is available, the normal serving path applies and the request may experience cold-start semantics (but with fallback policies available).
- Pre-warm actions: model binary resident in GPU memory, warmed CUDA kernels compiled, KV cache primed for most-common prefixes where applicable, and lightweight model-validation warm runs executed to avoid JIT stalls.
- Integration: warm-pool management surfaces as an optional flag on Dedicated purchase and as an add-on to Redwood Private via the control plane agent. Warm pools honor tenant isolation and RBAC rules.

Technical constraints & compatibility table:

| Feature | Hosted API | Dedicated | Private (VPC/on-prem) | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| GPU-backed warm slots | Yes (hosted reservations) | Yes | Yes | Hardware must support pinned pages and device residency policies |
| Quantized-only variants | Partial | Yes | Depends on platform | Some quantization pipelines require extra warm steps |
| Multi-model on single GPU | No | Yes | Configurable | Requires shard-aware warm placement |
| Edge / lightweight runtime | No | No | Limited | Not recommended for <GPU edge targets> |

Pricing model (high-level):

Pricing must balance predictable revenue and clear ROI for customers. Proposed tiers:

- Warm Unit: unit of 1 warm slot for 1 model family (monthly commitment). Warm Unit price varies by hardware class (A100, H100, or vCPU pool). Example list price (US dollars):
  1. A100-class slot: $7,500 / month (per slot)
  2. H100-class slot: $11,500 / month
  3. vCPU warm slot (for small LMs): $1,200 / month

- Minimum commitment: 2 Warm Units for monthly plans, discounts for annual commitment (20% off).
- Burst credits: each subscription includes 200 burst assignments per slot per month; additional bursts billed at per-request microcredits.
- Metering: metered by configured slot-count, active assignments, and burst overage. Billing report exposes: reserved slots, active-hours consumed, bursts consumed, and model-family tags.

Pricing examples (illustrative):

- Small SaaS: 2 A100 warm slots monthly = $15,000 / month (expected to reduce customer tail latency and replace expensive overprovisioning by ~40%).
- Mid-market: 5 vCPU warm slots (for quantized LMs) annual = 5 * $1,200 * 12 * 0.8 = $57,600 effective yearly.

SLA and SLO impact:

- Warm-capacity subscription includes an SLO for warm-assignment availability: 99.9% of warm assignment attempts must return within 100 ms for matching routes. This is scoped to the control plane and routing logic; model runtime and hardware failures are covered by existing Dedicated SLAs.
- Error budget accounting: warm-availability SLOs are tracked independently; warm subscription refunds (credits) are applied when monthly warm-availability < 99.9% following the standard credits playbook.

Telemetry and observability:

Required telemetry signals (exposed in Redwood Console):
- warm_slots_reserved (gauge per-tenant)
- warm_assignment_latency_ms (p95, p99)
- warm_burst_consumed (counter)
- warm_slot_efficiency (active-assignment-hours / reserved-hours)
- cold_start_rate_on_matching_routes (rate)

Reports to surface in Console:
- Warm capacity utilization heatmap (by hour, by model family)
- Cost-saving estimation: baseline cold-start penalty vs. warm-subscription cost per month
- Per-route tail-latency improvement attribution

Operational Playbook (on-call and failure scenarios):

1) Warm assignment fails (no slot): controller retries up to 3 times with exponential backoff, then falls back to normal serving with a tagged cold-start event. Alert: SRE warm-assignment-failure-rate > 0.5% sustained for 15 minutes.
2) Slot becomes unhealthy: drain slot, kick off replacement pre-warm, mark slot as degraded. Ownership: serving-runtime team.
3) Over-subscription detected: if warm-slot-efficiency < 20% for >7 days, trigger notification to customer success and propose downscale.

Launch plan and go-to-market playbook (90 days):

- Phase 0 (30 days): Beta with 6 strategic customers. Deliverables: console UI mock, billing schema, beta contract addendum, SLO measurement dashboards.
- Phase 1 (30 days): Public launch to Dedicated customers with self-serve purchase for monthly plans. SaaS docs, solutions playbook, SDK flags for warm preference.
- Phase 2 (30 days): Private deployment support, annual pricing, and field enablement with sales kits and ROI calculator.

Rollout checklist (operational & engineering):

1. Control plane: warm-pool subscription CRUD APIs and RBAC scoping.
2. Runtime: slot reservation protocol, pre-warm steps, and health-check instrumentation.
3. Billing: new invoice line item, usage exporter, and burst overage meter.
4. Console: dashboard tiles, utilization charts, and purchase workflow.
5. Legal: template addendum, terms for refunds/credits, and SLA text.
6. Customer Success: onboarding runbook, playbook for sizing recommendations, and escalation matrix.

Implementation requirements (developer-facing):

- API contract example (JSON payload):

  {
    "subscription_name": "team-x-warmpool-1",
    "slots": 3,
    "model_tags": ["llama-2-70b", "redwood-verified-gpt-compat"],
    "hardware_class": "A100",
    "burst_credit_policy": { "included_bursts_per_slot_month": 200 }
  }

- Config flags: enable_warm_pool_routes=true, warm_assignment_timeout_ms=100, warm_health_probe_interval_s=30
- Backward compatibility: warm pools must not change default routing for customers who do not opt in.

Open questions & decisions required:

- Pricing elasticity: should burst overage be metered in microcredits or token-based units? Decision impacts billing plumbing.
- Slot accounting granularity: per-VM vs per-GPU shard for multi-model placements.
- Support for ephemeral warm reservations tied to scheduled events (e.g., daily demos): immediate vs delayed billing adjustments.

Risks and mitigations:

- Risk: Customers overbuy warm slots and underutilize, leading to churn. Mitigation: offer 14-day trial and utilization-based recommendations in Console.
- Risk: Complexity across Private/on-prem installations. Mitigation: ship a lightweight control-plane agent and a validated installer matrix for supported hardware.

Appendix: sample customer sizing worksheet (text table)

| Customer traffic profile | 95th token/sec | Estimated cold-start penalty (ms) | Recommended warm slots | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Interactive chat, 500 users concurrent | 250 tps | 320 ms | 2 A100 slots | Warm slots assigned by route grouping |
| Batch reranker, periodic peaks | 50 tps | 120 ms | 1 vCPU slot | Consider scheduled pre-warm windows |
